pages.title: Connect. Measure. Calibrate.
pages.text:
ESP32-S3 / A3-120 / BUILD & SERVICE MANUAL
Connect. Measure. Calibrate.
Sensor installation, connection diagnosis and ECU Studio configuration
120 × 120 mm through-hole carrier • Plug-in ESP32-S3 DevKitC-1 • Revision A3-120 / 30 October 2026
Engineering prototype and bench monitor. All actuator commands remain OFF. This package does not implement a
complete replacement engine ECU and has not been tested on a car. CAD checks and software tests do not establish
surge immunity, EMC, splash resistance, emissions compliance or mechanical fit.
Read in this order
01
Identify the board revision, connector orientation and power arrangement.
02
Assemble and test the unpowered board, then qualify the power rails on a current-limited bench supply.
03
Use the individual sensor chapters and identical web guides. Enter the real sensor curves, then verify independent
reference points.
04
Fit the insulating tray, shield bonds and splash gasket. Check the printed fit and controlled splash resistance before
choosing any installation location.

pages.title: What this design supports
pages.text:
01 / SCOPE
What this design supports
 Implemented
Outside this release
Six conditioned 0-5 V analog inputs, 12-bit SPI ADC, diagnostic
conversion and filtering.
Fuel/ignition scheduling, fuel maps, tune commissioning, knock
control and engine operation.
Two conditioned 5 V Hall inputs, missing-tooth crank bench
decoder and cam edge counts.
Raw VR sensors, full 720° phase decoding, every OEM trigger
pattern.
500 kbit/s listen-only CAN frame counts.
OEM CAN messages, dashboard, immobilizer, automatic
transmission or air-conditioning integration.
External wideband-controller analog input and buffered
post-catalyst measurement.
Raw wideband drive/heater control, catalyst efficiency diagnostics
and OBD emissions readiness.
Design provisions for surge clamping, reverse polarity, filtering,
ground plane and shield return.
Verified ISO automotive transient/EMC qualification or universal
compatibility.
Universal carrier, vehicle-specific interface
01
There is no universal OEM ECU connector or sensor pinout. Use a documented adapter harness with verified cavity
numbers for the specific vehicle.
02
A naturally aspirated engine with a catalytic converter can still require electronic throttle, immobilizer and network
functions absent here. Keep the original ECU in service until an actual replacement system is separately engineered
and qualified.
03
Do not share sensor signals with another ECU until input loading, grounding and failure behavior have been
reviewed. Do not remove or emulate catalyst monitoring.
Basic bench kit
01
Current-limited regulated 12 V supply, suitable 1 A external fuse and an accessible disconnect.
02
Digital multimeter, magnifier, soldering iron and appropriate leaded soldering tools. Use a properly referenced or
isolated oscilloscope for digital edges and noise.
03
3.3 V UART adapter; do not use 5 V TTL, RS-232 levels or an adapter power lead.
04
A trusted low-voltage signal/reference source and sensor-specific mechanical/reference tools. Never use a test lamp
on a signal input.

pages.title: Build and inspect the carrier
pages.text:
02 / BOARD ASSEMBLY
Build and inspect the carrier
01
Use hardware/a3-compact, not the larger A2 board. The copper outline is 120 × 120 mm, six copper layers, 1.6 mm
nominal FR-4. Check the final ERC/DRC and audit reports before ordering.
02
All carrier component joints are plated through-hole. Fit ordinary axial resistors upright on the indicated 2.54 mm
pitch; R150 stays horizontal. Observe the vertical diode polarity drawing, not just the direction of a bent lead.
03
Fit low components first, then capacitors, direct-solder DIP ICs, TO-220 devices and connectors. IC sockets are not
required. Leave DNP optional pull-ups absent unless the specific sensor needs them.
04
Fit the two 1 × 22 female headers for the specified 44-pin ESP32-S3 DevKitC-1 v1.1. Use a known straight header
jig while soldering. Do not substitute a similar-looking 30/38-pin ESP32 or assume every S3 board has the same
spacing.
05
U1 is a purchased assembled Pololu D36V6F5 module. U3 is a purchased DevKit. These modules contain small
factory-soldered parts; no bare S3 module or fine-pitch IC must be hand-soldered to the carrier.
06
Check IC notches, electrolytic polarity, diode bands, transistor pin order and live TO-220 tabs against the BOM and
footprints. VNP35N07-E tabs are drain, not ground.
07
Inspect every joint, bridge and solder splash. Trim solder tails to at most 3 mm below the PCB, especially around
H4. The printed H4 support includes reliefs matching R35 and D210.
08
With power disconnected, check for unintended rail shorts. Capacitors can make a continuity buzzer sound briefly;
investigate sustained low resistance rather than relying on the buzzer alone.
The 120 mm layout is dense. A 3D model may omit an unavailable manufacturer model; the BOM, assembly drawing
and native footprint pads define the build. DNP resistors are intentionally empty. Never infer that a pad is unused
simply because a 3D body is absent.
EMI provisions are an assembly requirement
01
Retain the two continuous inner ground planes and the input filter/clamps. Keep sensor returns separate from the
actuator power-return wiring.
02
Use twisted/shielded signal wiring as appropriate to the sensor. Keep it away from ignition coils, alternator wiring
and relay/motor power.
03
Fit the conductive enclosure lining and short internal shield bonds, then cover the lining with the supplied dielectric
tray and lid insulator. A plastic box alone is not an RF shield.

pages.title: Check power before sensors
pages.text:
03 / FIRST POWER
Check power before sensors
01
Pin 1 is externally fused key-on 12 V; pin 2 is ground. Use the specified external 1 A source fuse.
02
For first bench checks, unplug every sensor and actuator, keep J3 open, use a 12 V current-limited supply, and
check polarity before enabling it.
03
Measure TP2 VIN_PROT, TP3 5 V, TP4 3V3, then each sensor pin 2. TP2 is after the reverse diode and before the
input filter.
04
Repeated resets can be undervoltage/current limit, a short, wrong part orientation, regulator instability or watchdog
timeout. Disconnect external loads one at a time.
Point
Meaning
Expected bench observation
TP1
GND
Reference for board checks.
TP2
VIN_PROT
Input after reverse diode, before input filter. At a 12 V source it is lower than the
source by the diode drop.
TP3
+5V
Near nominal 5 V; verify under the intended sensor load.
TP4
+3V3
Near nominal 3.3 V; measure U6 VREF accurately for calibration.
TP5
SAFE_N
Near 3V3 when released; low during supervisor/watchdog reset.
TP6
RUN_5V
Low with J3 open and configuration monitor firmware.
If a rail is wrong
01
Disconnect external harnesses and remove the DevKit, then locate the fault from the input toward the load. Check
part value/orientation, the reverse diode and buck module pinout.
02
If 5 V collapses only with a sensor plugged in, check its actual pin order and current draw. The sensor rail PTC is
shared, slow and temperature-dependent, not a precision electronic current limiter.
03
If 3V3 resets or overheats during Wi-Fi, inspect regulator dissipation, supply limits, capacitor/ESR requirements and
current peaks. Software compilation does not verify power integrity.
04
Scope rails, SAFE_N and WDI together for repeating resets. Do not bypass the watchdog or supervisor. The
monitor must keep servicing supervision while the web service runs.
J1 powers the ECU logic. Injector, smart-coil and relay power is external, fused and relay-switched. Do not connect an
engine or real actuator harness during these checks.

pages.title: Open ECU Studio
pages.text:
04 / WEB SERVICE
Open ECU Studio
01
Flash the compact_a3_web firmware using PlatformIO. Remove the DevKit from the carrier before powering its USB
connector. Disconnect USB before reseating it in the unpowered carrier.
02
Keep J3 open and actuator harnesses disconnected. Attach J2 UART using 3.3 V logic at 115200 baud, 8-N-1, with
no adapter power wire.
03
Power the carrier on a dry bench with the lid open. The service starts its own WPA2 AP, ECU-Service-XXXX. A new
random password is printed in the UART boot log.
04
Join that AP and open http://192.168.4.1. No internet connection is needed. The AP is refused if J3 is closed at
service startup. The conductive lining may block radio reception with the lid closed.
05
For a desktop preview, run python3 tools/web_server.py and open http://127.0.0.1:8765. The simulator is labelled
NO HARDWARE and uses synthetic ADC values.
Screenshot: the actual offline UI running against the host simulator. Example numbers shown are not a vehicle calibration.
Save and preserve settings
01
Export a JSON backup before editing. Import stages a complete validated profile in the editor; it does not apply until
saved.
02
Save validates all channels and commits NVS before changing the live conversion. Check the saved revision and
status message.
03
A stale revision is rejected instead of overwriting another session. Export edits, reload the latest profile and reapply
the intended change.
04
Unreadable or invalid saved storage activates defaults and blocks saving. Inspect UART and recover deliberately;
firmware does not erase NVS automatically.

pages.title: Configure a measured transfer curve
pages.text:
05 / CALIBRATION
Configure a measured transfer curve
01
Voltage mode shows the reconstructed connector voltage; it does not require a sensor transfer curve.
02
Linear mode uses two measured input voltages and two physical values. Set the actual units and validate a third
reference point.
03
Table mode interpolates between 2-16 ascending voltage/value pairs. Values outside the table range are faults, not
extrapolated measurements.
04
NTC beta mode is for CLT/IAT only and requires the physical pull-up. It uses the measured sensor supply and
compensates the 55 kohm divider load. A voltage table is preferable when the real curve is available.
05
Filtering is for readout smoothing, not a substitute for fixing wiring/noise. Electrical fault checks use the
instantaneous input.
06
A saved sensor profile changes diagnostic readout only. Engine scheduling, DBW, injector tuning, catalyst
diagnostics and OEM protocols are not implemented.
07
Trigger geometry is applied to the bench decoder when configuration is saved. Crank synchronization is 360
degrees only.
A practical calibration sequence
01
Choose the sensor connector, verify supply/ground and compare displayed connector voltage with a trusted meter.
Correct wiring before changing a curve.
02
Measure the actual ADC reference and enter it under Device & profile. A reference error changes every
reconstructed voltage, including battery and sensor supply.
03
Choose voltage, two-point linear, voltage table or supported NTC beta. Enter physical units consistently. Use the
real manufacturer curve or independently measured references, never the illustrative simulator curve.
04
Set an input fault window appropriate to that specific sensor. The default window is a starting point, not a diagnosis
of every open/short. A legitimate endpoint can be zero volts on some interfaces.
05
Choose only as much readout filtering as necessary. Inspect raw voltage and the oscilloscope signal while checking
wiring noise.
06
Save, verify several independent points across the intended range and only then mark the calibration confirmed.
Record the sensor part number, curve source, pull-up and reference tools.
Mode
Fields and behavior
Voltage
Reconstructs connector volts: ADC / 4095 × measured VREF / 0.6.
Linear
V0/Y0 and V1/Y1; ascending voltage endpoints. Physical values can increase or decrease. Outside the endpoints
is a fault.
Table
2-16 ascending voltage/value pairs. Piecewise linear interpolation. No extrapolation beyond the table.
NTC beta
CLT/IAT only. R0, reference temperature, beta and actual physical pull-up. Uses measured sensor supply and 55
kohm load compensation.
Fault/filter
Fault checks use instantaneous voltage. The display filter smooths readout, not engine control.

Before connecting any sensor
01
Board pin numbers refer to the PCB top view; pin 1 is the square pad. The mating plug view can be mirrored. Verify
the actual harness with continuity tests.
02
Disconnect power before resistance/continuity tests. Do not measure resistance on a live vehicle bus or use a
megohmmeter on electronics.
03
Keep J3 open and all actuator harnesses disconnected during sensor commissioning. This firmware keeps ARM off.
04
Use the actual sensor or controller manufacturer pinout, transfer curve, mounting torque and air gap. There is no
universal vehicle-side pinout.
05
Measure signal voltage against that sensor connector pin 1, not an arbitrary chassis bolt. Never use a test lamp on a
sensor or MCU pin.
Passive two-wire CLT/IAT NTCs use pins 1 and 3 only. Wideband-controller analog outputs use pins 1 and 3; pin 2
does not power a heater/controller. Raw VR and raw LSU sensors are unsupported without the appropriate external
interface.

pages.title: MAP / manifold pressure
pages.text:
07.1 / J11
MAP / manifold pressure
 PIN 1
PIN 2
PIN 3
1 GND
2 SENSOR_5V
3 MAP
Mounting & routing
01
Retain the OEM pressure port or use a suitable sealed manifold-pressure takeoff after the throttle. Keep the hose
short and secure, and follow the sensor maker's fluid/orientation limits.
02
Route away from hot exhaust and ignition wiring. Leak-check any added hose before running an engine.
Connect & verify
01
Confirm the sensor uses 5 V and identify its actual supply, ground and signal wires from its datasheet.
02
With power off, check each harness conductor end-to-end and for unintended shorts, with both ends unplugged.
03
Power the board, check pin 2 near 5 V, then connect the sensor and measure pin 3 versus pin 1.
04
Use a regulated hand vacuum/pressure source within the sensor rating, compare the web voltage with a meter, then
enter the manufacturer transfer curve or measured reference points.
Expected behavior
01
Key-on / engine-off pressure should agree with a trusted local absolute-pressure reference after calibration. It is not
always 100 kPa.
02
A steady applied pressure should produce a steady voltage and calibrated value.
Fault tracing
01
Flat near 0 V: inspect power, ground, signal short and sensor pin order.
02
Flat high: inspect a short to supply, wrong curve, or a saturated sensor.
03
Pressure wrong but voltage agrees with the meter: check absolute versus gauge units, curve and pressure
reference.
04
Noisy or slow: inspect hose leaks/restriction, ground offset, shield routing and configured filtering.
R20 22k series, R21 33k to ground, C20 10nF; U6 channel 0.

pages.title: TPS / throttle position
pages.text:
07.2 / J12
TPS / throttle position
 PIN 1
PIN 2
PIN 3
1 GND
2 SENSOR_5V
3 TPS
Mounting & routing
01
Use the OEM TPS mounting and its correct shaft coupling. A single analog input does not replace an electronic
throttle system or its redundant safety channels.
02
Turn the throttle only with the vehicle made safe; do not force an electronic throttle plate or alter mechanical stops.
Connect & verify
01
Identify whether the TPS is a 3-wire potentiometer or another sensor. Do not connect throttle-motor wires to J12.
02
Verify pin 2 supply and pin 1 ground, then observe signal voltage while moving the permitted mechanism slowly.
03
Record closed and fully open reference voltages, enter those as 0% and 100%, and mark calibration confirmed only
after checking the whole travel.
Expected behavior
01
The voltage should sweep smoothly without dropouts. Some sensors have a decreasing transfer curve; configure
the corresponding endpoint values.
Fault tracing
01
Jumps at one position: inspect sensor track/coupling or a broken harness conductor.
02
Direction reversed: swap calibration endpoint values, not supply and ground wires.
03
Does not reach 0%/100%: recheck mechanical travel and measured endpoints.
04
Two TPS tracks or a throttle motor are present: this hardware does not implement OEM DBW control.
R22 22k series, R23 33k to ground, C21 10nF; U6 channel 1.

pages.title: Coolant temperature
pages.text:
07.3 / J13
Coolant temperature
 PIN 1
PIN 2
PIN 3
1 GND
2 SENSOR_5V
3 CLT
Mounting & routing
01
Use the OEM coolant sensor and mounting boss, with the engine cold and cooling system depressurized. Follow the
specified seal and torque.
02
Keep the original vehicle sensor if required by other systems; verify loading before sharing any signal.
Connect & verify
01
For a passive two-wire NTC, use pins 1 and 3 only. Leave pin 2 empty in the mating housing.
02
Fit R32 only if this is a passive NTC requiring the board pull-up. Check its actual resistance; the design value is 2.49
kohm.
03
Measure sensor resistance while disconnected and compare at known temperatures with its datasheet. Prefer
several reference points.
04
Enter beta parameters or a voltage table. In NTC mode, confirm the physical pull-up is fitted; the UI cannot install a
resistor.
Expected behavior
01
A common NTC resistance falls as temperature rises, and its signal voltage falls with this pull-up topology.
02
The conversion accounts for the board's 55 kohm divider load and measured sensor supply.
Fault tracing
01
Near 0 V: sensor/loom short to ground or very low resistance.
02
High signal / open-model fault: unplugged sensor, broken ground/signal or missing/wrong pull-up.
03
Plausible voltage but wrong temperature: wrong NTC curve, pull-up value, supply reading or units.
04
Do not assume a floating/unexcited input will read maximum voltage: R32 is DNP by default.
R24 22k series, R25 33k to ground, C22 10nF; U6 channel 2.
R32 is DNP by default. Fit it only after confirming the actual sensor topology and resistor value.

Intake-air temperature

PIN 2
PIN 3
1 GND

Mounting & routing
01
Use a suitable intake-air boss and the sensor maker's orientation. Avoid placing the sensing element against the
intake wall or at an unrepresentative heat source.
02
Follow the original mechanical arrangement; secure any aftermarket sensor so it cannot enter the intake.
Connect & verify
01
A passive two-wire NTC connects to pins 1 and 3; pin 2 remains empty.
02
R33 is the optional board pull-up, normally 2.49 kohm. Confirm it is physically fitted before using NTC conversion.
03
Compare disconnected resistance and stabilized readings with a reference thermometer at several temperatures.
Enter the actual sensor curve.
Expected behavior
01
After a long cold soak, intake and coolant temperature should be reasonably consistent with their actual
surroundings. Heat soak can produce real differences.
Fault tracing
01
Use the same open/short/pull-up checks as CLT, but inspect intake heat soak and airflow before blaming calibration.
02
Fast spikes suggest intermittent wires or electrical interference. A slow heat-soak drift may be physical.

Wideband controller output

PIN 2
PIN 3
1 GND
2 SENSOR_5V

Mounting & routing
01
Install the exhaust sensor according to the sensor/controller maker's rules for bung angle, temperature and
condensation. The ECU board does not heat or drive a raw wideband sensor.
02
Mount the external controller away from hot exhaust and splash paths; use its specified fused power and grounds.
Connect & verify
01
Connect controller analog signal to pin 3 and its specified analog reference to pin 1.
02
Leave pin 2 unpopulated; the board sensor supply must not power the controller or heater.

Use the controller's documented analog-output test mode or a known voltage source before interpreting exhaust
readings.
Expected behavior
01
Web voltage and a meter should agree; converted lambda should agree with the controller when both use the same
mapping and ground reference.
Fault tracing
01
Controller display correct but ECU wrong: inspect mapping, analog-reference offset and output mode.
02
Fixed fault voltage: read the external controller's error codes before treating it as mixture.
03
No output until heated: verify controller state and heater supply.
04
A raw LSU sensor cannot be connected directly; do not invent a direct 5-wire/6-wire pin mapping.

pages.text:

Buffered post-catalyst signal
 PIN 1
PIN 2
PIN 3
1 GND
2 SENSOR_5V

Mounting & routing
01
Retain the catalyst and rear oxygen sensor in their proper locations. This input is for measurement, not catalyst
emulation or bypass.
02
Use a suitable external high-input-impedance conditioner/buffer where needed. The board input presents about 55
kohm to the sensor signal.

01
Connect only the buffer's conditioned 0-5 V output to pin 3 and its analog reference to pin 1. Leave pin 2 empty

02

load.
03
Compare the buffer output with a meter; enter its transfer curve or retain voltage display.
Expected behavior
01
Voltage is the directly supported diagnostic. This firmware does not implement catalyst-efficiency monitoring,
emissions readiness or OEM rear-sensor diagnostics.
Fault tracing
01
Signal changes when shared with OEM ECU: stop and review input loading and the buffer interface.
02
Zero or clipped output: inspect buffer supply/reference and output limits.
03
A stable rear reading alone does not prove catalyst health.

pages.title: Crank Hall input
pages.text:
08.1 / J17
Crank Hall input
 PIN 1
PIN 2
PIN 3
1 GND
2 SENSOR_5V
3 CRANK_RAW
Mounting & routing
01
Use the original rigid bracket/target-wheel relationship and the exact manufacturer air gap, polarity, supply rating
and torque. There is no universal trigger gap.
02
This input accepts a compatible 5 V Hall interface. A two-wire variable-reluctance sensor needs an external
conditioner.
Connect & verify
01
Verify supply and ground before connecting. Determine whether the Hall output is push-pull or open-collector.
02
For an open-collector output without another suitable pull-up, fit the specified optional pull-up and verify the
current/voltage requirements.
03
Use an oscilloscope to compare connector pin 3 with the conditioned MCU input. A multimeter can miss missing
pulses and noise.
04
With ignition/injection disabled, turn the target safely or use an isolated bench signal generator. Do not connect a
generator in parallel with an energized sensor.
Expected behavior
01
Only rising edges are captured. Both signal paths use two Schmitt inversions, preserving the input polarity.
02
Crank sync requires the selected missing-tooth geometry and repeated valid gaps. Cam is counted but full
720-degree phase decoding is not implemented.
Fault tracing
01
No edges: inspect supply, missing pull-up, wrong sensor type, target gap, signal/ground pin order and U7
conditioning.
02
Edges but no sync: inspect total slots/missing teeth, speed range, signal quality and electrical noise. A simple
square wave is not a valid missing-tooth wheel.
03
False RPM / overflow: inspect ringing, shield/return routing, gap and pull-up; power-cycle after a latched capture
overflow.
R40 33k series, C30 100pF, optional R41 2.2k pull-up; U7 -> GPIO8.

pages.title: Power, data and output connections
pages.text:
09.1 / SERVICE INTERFACES
Power, data and output connections
J1 / Logic power
01
Pin 1 is externally fused key-on 12 V; pin 2 is ground. Use the specified external 1 A source fuse.
02
For first bench checks, unplug every sensor and actuator, keep J3 open, use a 12 V current-limited supply, and
check polarity before enabling it.
03
Measure TP2 VIN_PROT, TP3 5 V, TP4 3V3, then each sensor pin 2. TP2 is after the reverse diode and before the
input filter.
04
Repeated resets can be undervoltage/current limit, a short, wrong part orientation, regulator instability or watchdog
timeout. Disconnect external loads one at a time.
J2 / UART / boot / reset
01
Pins: 1 ground, 2 ECU TX -> adapter RX, 3 ECU RX <- adapter TX, 4 EN, 5 BOOT_N. Use 3.3 V logic, 115200
baud, 8-N-1.
02
Do not connect an adapter power wire or a powered DevKit USB cable while the carrier supplies the module. For
USB programming, remove the module from the carrier.
03
If silent, check supply and EN, cross TX/RX correctly, verify the A3 build and chosen serial port, then capture the
boot log. The existing console tag can still say ecu_a0.
04
For ROM download mode, hold BOOT_N low during an EN reset, then release it. Do not short EN or BOOT_N to 12
V.

pages.title: Power, data and output connections
pages.text:
09.2 / SERVICE INTERFACES
Power, data and output connections
J3 / Physical interlock
01
Pin 1 is 3V3 and pin 2 is INTERLOCK. Open is the normal state during commissioning.
02
lock=0 with the contact open is expected. Closing it can allow hardware run gating; do not close it with vehicle
actuators connected.
03
The configuration firmware keeps ARM=0 regardless. Never bypass SAFE_N to make a fault disappear.
J4 / Internal expansion
01
Pins: ground / 3V3 / SDA / SCL / SAFE_N. This is an internal 3.3 V service bus, not a 12 V sensor connector.
02
Check pull-ups and idle SDA/SCL near 3V3. A stuck-low line suggests a short, wrong device voltage or a device
holding the bus.
03
No generic external I2C scanner or expansion actuator control is implemented by this release.

pages.title: Power, data and output connections
pages.text:
09.3 / SERVICE INTERFACES
Power, data and output connections
J7 / JP1 / JP2 / CAN and termination
01
J7: CANH / CANL / ground / CHASSIS. Keep the pair twisted and verify the network bitrate. Firmware reception is
500 kbit/s listen-only; no OEM decoding is provided.
02
JP1 open leaves MCP2562 in standby, so ordinary frames will not be received. Close it only on the appropriate
supervised bus for normal transceiver reception. Firmware remains listen-only.
03
JP2 adds onboard 120 ohm termination when closed. Leave it open on an already terminated vehicle network.
04
With the complete network unpowered, two 120 ohm end terminations normally measure about 60 ohm between
CANH and CANL. A removed/unpowered interface alone need not read 60 ohm.
05
No frames: inspect JP1, bitrate, polarity, grounds, bus activity and termination. A standalone two-node listen-only
bench cannot supply missing ACKs for a lone transmitter.
J8 / External relay coils
01
Pins: MAIN low side / PUMP low side / FAN low side / ground. External fused relay supplies and correctly oriented
flyback diodes are required.
02
Target coil current is at most 150 mA per channel, pending physical tests. Do not connect a fan motor or pump
motor directly.
03
The configuration firmware commands all channels OFF. An inactive relay is expected, not a reason to bypass the
inhibit.
04
With a coil connected to a safe test supply, OFF low-side voltage can be near the external supply, not zero.
Driver/tab is electrically live. Actuation tests require a separate qualified dummy-load procedure.

pages.title: Power, data and output connections
pages.text:
09.4 / SERVICE INTERFACES
Power, data and output connections
J9 / J19 / Injector outputs and power return
01
J9 pins 1-4 are injector low sides 1-4; pins 5-8 are ground. J19 both pins are the dedicated power return.
02
Only saturated high-impedance PFI injectors are in scope; 1.2 A/channel is a design target pending tests. No GDI or
peak-and-hold driver is provided.
03
Actuator 12 V is external, fused and relay switched. Never use the sensor ground harness as the injector current
return.
04
All outputs remain OFF in this firmware. Check resistance/continuity only disconnected; do not pulse a fueled engine
to troubleshoot wiring.
05
A high OFF output with an externally powered load is normal. Persistent current with ARM off indicates wrong
wiring, a shorted driver or a board fault: disconnect power.
J10 / Smart-coil logic only
01
Pins 1-4 are active-high 5 V smart-coil commands; pin 5 is ground. They are not ignition-coil primary outputs.
02
Use only a compatible low-current logic input (design target at most 4 mA). Coil power and power-ground wiring
remain external.
03
The configuration firmware keeps dwell commands OFF. Do not use a test lamp, an ordinary LED without its
resistor, or a coil primary as a logic test load.
04
Changing or interrupting dwell on a real coil can produce a spark. Keep real ignition hardware disconnected during
bench configuration.

pages.title: Power, data and output connections
pages.text:
09.5 / SERVICE INTERFACES
Power, data and output connections
J20 / H5 / Shield and enclosure bond
01
J20 pins and plated lug H5 are CHASSIS, not normal sensor/actuator current returns. Bond them to the internal
lining using the assembly guide.
02
Check lining/braid continuity with power off. The CHASSIS-to-GND 1 Mohm bleed and 4.7 nF RF capacitor are
intentional, not a hard DC ground link.
03
Keep all bonds inside the water seal and route any external reference conductor through a sealed gland. Do not drill
an unsealed shield-stud hole.
TP1-TP6 / Test points
01
TP1 ground; TP2 VIN_PROT; TP3 5 V; TP4 3V3; TP5 SAFE_N; TP6 RUN_5V.
02
With J3 open and monitor firmware, RUN_5V should be low even when supplies are healthy. SAFE_N is an
open-drain supervised net, normally pulled near 3V3 when released.
03
If SAFE_N repeatedly drops, scope it with the supply rails and WDI. Do not defeat the MAX1232 or 3V3 supervisor.
04
Use a properly referenced or isolated scope arrangement; do not clip an earth-referenced scope ground to an
arbitrary live output.

pages.title: Trace a fault from the connector inward
pages.text:
10 / LIVE DIAGNOSIS
Trace a fault from the connector inward
Screenshot: host simulator with a deliberately shorted MAP input. Fault-injection controls are absent from the embedded firmware.
01
Start with battery and sensor-rail measurements. If several channels fail together, inspect shared power/ground
before adjusting every curve.
02
Compare pin 3 versus pin 1 at the connector with the web connector voltage. If those agree, inspect curve, units and
reference settings.
03
If connector voltage is correct but ADC is wrong, check the named 22k/33k input divider, clamp polarity, filter
capacitor, U6 reference and SPI connections. Do not inject an automotive battery voltage as a signal test.
04
If all ADC channels are stuck at zero/full scale, inspect U6 power/reference, chip select, MOSI/MISO/clock, solder
bridges and the live ADC transfer status. A successful SPI transaction alone cannot prove sensor integrity.
05
For missing crank/cam counts, scope both raw and conditioned signals. Review pull-ups, Hall-versus-VR type,
target geometry and air gap before blaming software.
06
Capture overflow is latched until power cycle. Find the signal/queue cause first; clearing a latch does not repair the
source.
07
Export the diagnostic report with timestamp, profile revision and browser event history. Event history starts when
that browser session starts. The export is not a persistent ECU flight recorder.
08
If the page disconnects, readings become stale. Check the AP, board supply and UART, then reconnect. Never use
a frozen browser number as a live measurement.

pages.title: Install the board and shield
pages.text:
11 / PRINTED ENCLOSURE
Install the board and shield
PCB: 120 × 120 mm. Printed base: 138 × 150 × 44 mm. Lid: 142 × 154 mm. Nominal assembled height: 47 mm. Cable glands add to the
rear envelope.
01
Print base, lid, insulating tray, lid insulator and insert coupon. Use a material/process suitable for the measured
installation temperature, chemicals and vibration. Do not assume a printed case is suitable beside an exhaust or
underhood heat source.
02
Test the coupon with the actual short M3 heat-set inserts before fitting them to the case. Four PCB supports take M3
short inserts; eight lid bosses and two internal shield bonds use the same insert type.
03
Install the internal base shield-bond insert and lining before the PCB blocks tool access. Keep the side-wall bond
blind: do not drill through the outer wall.
04
Apply conductive lining following the templates. Keep it below and clear of the water-seal land. Bond seams with a
suitable conductive method and use short broad internal bonds. The gasket is not an electrical bond.
05
Fit the insulating tray over the lining. Clear the support roots and internal bond boss. Ensure conductive foil cannot
touch solder tails, module pins, live transistor tabs or terminals.
06
Install the PCB at box origin 9,9 mm and Z=9 mm. Hole centers are (13,13), (125,13), (13,125), (125,125) mm from
the base origin. Use four M3 × 6 screws and 0.8 mm nylon washers.
07
Trim all solder tails to at most 3 mm below the PCB. H4 has specific relief pockets for R35 and D210; align the board
correctly and confirm the tail clearances by dry fitting.
08
Dry fit all mating plugs, wire bends and strain relief with the unpowered board. Do not force a cable against the lid, a
live transistor tab or the gasket. The CAD component envelope does not qualify the finished harness.
09
Fit the removable lid lining bond and its dielectric cover. Leave a flexible internal bond loop that cannot snag, touch
electronics or cross the gasket.

pages.title: Seal the lid and cable entries
pages.text:
12 / SPLASH RESISTANCE
Seal the lid and cable entries
01
Cut one continuous ring from 2.0 mm soft closed-cell silicone sheet with the supplied 1:1 template. The ring is 3 mm
wide; the groove is 3.4 mm wide and 1.5 mm deep. Do not print the reference gasket in ordinary rigid filament.
02
Inspect the sealing land, groove, case walls and layers for pores, strings and damage. Establish a compatible
sealing/post-processing method if the printing process leaves porous walls.
03
Seat the ring without stretches, twists, gaps or adhesive lumps. The nominal geometry compresses a 2 mm sheet to
1.5 mm (25%); check the actual chosen material and print dimensions.
04
Fit four suitable M16 cable glands, or gasketed blanking plugs for unused holes. Their panel flange must fit the 24
mm diameter envelope. Use the manufacturer sealing washers and cable-jacket diameter range.
05
A single-hole gland seals against a round cable jacket, not a bundle of loose individual wires. Use appropriately
jacketed multi-core harness groups and sealed external branches. The JST connectors are inside the box and are
not sealed external bulkhead connectors.
06
Provide harness strain relief and a drip loop. Place cable entries away from direct splash and pooling. The rear entry
centers are X=27,55,83,111 mm and Z=27 mm.
07
Close the lid with its drip skirt outside the base wall. Use eight M3 × 8 screws with 0.8 mm washers, tighten evenly
and inspect continuous gasket seating. Screw holes lie outside the nominal water-seal line.
08
Test the empty assembled case with absorbent paper before installing electronics. Start with controlled light
splashes in the intended orientations, inspect every seam and gland, dry completely, and correct leaks before
repeating. No IP rating or pressure-wash/submersion capability is claimed.
Splash resistance, printed fit, insert strength, vibration, thermal behavior and shielding performance require physical
tests. The CAD checks prove nominal solid/mesh integrity and specified clearances only. Keep all service work dry;
opening the lid removes the splash barrier.
Hardware list
01
4 × M3 × 6 PCB screws and 0.8 mm nylon washers; 8 × M3 × 8 lid screws and 0.8 mm flat washers.
02
14 × ruthex RX-M3Sx4.0 short inserts: 4 PCB, 8 lid, 2 internal shield bonds. Check the actual insert datasheet and
printed coupon.
03
2 × M3 × 5 bond screws with suitable ring terminals/star washers; H5 uses a separate M3 bolt/nut and short braid.
04
2 mm closed-cell silicone gasket sheet, conductive lining/bond materials, four matched M16 glands or sealed
blanks.

Record the evidence for this build

measurement.

Separate qualification still needed
01
Measure reverse-polarity, supply transients/load dump, cranking brownout, regulator stability and thermal margins
with suitable controlled equipment.
02
Qualify sensor fault stress, clamp currents, output current/clamp/thermal behavior and hardware inhibition on
appropriate dummy loads.
03
Check EMC/immunity, grounding, harness interaction, vibration and environmental performance.
04
An actual vehicle ECU replacement needs a reviewed vehicle harness, complete engine control implementation and
calibration, safety analysis and applicable emissions/legal assessment.
